verdict.rationale: Crossmint documents user-owned, non-custodial agent wallets. The agent gets a delegated signer key under user-signed, onchain-enforced spend caps, counterparty limits and time windows, all revocable by the user. Funding is covered by onramp orders that deliver tokens into a specified wallet and by the 'funded Crossmint EVM wallet' prerequisite. However, explicit balance visibility is documented only for card order intents (total/reserved/spent/available), not for the wallet itself, so story coverage is incomplete. Missing for 10: documented wallet balance query/visibility for the user, independent or hands-on corroboration of the agent-wallet flow.

support.subject: As an AI-native user, I can provision a wallet my agent holds and spends from — funded and controlled by me, with balance visibility

citations.quote: The user owns a non-custodial wallet and grants the agent scoped permissions (spend limit, counterparties, time window), enforced onchain.
Create a user-owned smart wallet, authorize an agent as a delegated signer, and send USDXM on Base Sepolia.
The order returns a payment intent that the buyer completes to receive tokens in the specified wallet.
The order intent tracks the total, reserved, spent, and available amounts.
Wallet webhooks allow you to receive real-time notifications for events that occur on wallets in your project.
